correctness.rationale: Exact isotropic pair-distance moment expansion and normalized uniform-shell radial moments establish F_d. The strict convexity of x coth x proves global monotonicity, not just numerical positivity. Interval arithmetic gives the exact dimension-six collision condition and a constructive scale match; endpoint asymptotic calculations and a derivative lower-bound argument prove the inverse exponents and global Hölder limit. The actual verify.py file was executed with 2,122 successful checks, including independent point-pair simulations. No finite check is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies the exact information content of two natural Euclidean pair-distance moments for homogeneous hollow balls, including radius reconstruction, sharp feasible intervals, the first dimension-aliasing transition at six, exact overlap sizes, and two different endpoint stability exponents. These are motivated by inverse geometry of unlabeled point clouds, not an arbitrary numerical slice or already-known full-ball moment tabulation.
